title: [storage] storage.disk_fall's day figure reads each end as the median of a 6 h window of samples, so a gate holding build trees at one sample's minute no longer moves it
prompt:
Spawn, objective 228 [storage] (the lead's order of 2026-11-19 05:3x, from rev-i's 4/222 observation; rev-g's scope 05:4x; the lead's YES with three conditions on 222.sh; author rev-g; readers rev-b first, rev-h second): storage.disk_fall's day figure reads each end as the median of a 6 h window of samples, not one sample.

Why. Since objective 222, storage.disk_fall is the worse of the week's fit and the last day's fall, with its basis. The day's fall (crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/disk.rs, day_fall) is read from one host.core_lines sample, the latest a day old or more and no older than 36 h, to the one free disk read now.
- Samples are hourly (SPAWN_CORE_LINES_SAMPLE_SECS, default 3600).
- A gate holding build trees moves df's free disk by about 6 GB within 10 minutes (rev-i, 4/222: the journal's df 03:47 -> 03:57 on 11-18).
- So the figure, which worse() often says (basis "day"), moves by up to 6 GB a day depending on whether a gate held trees at either end's minute.
- On the lead's 99 live hourly samples (sync/obj-228-lead/free-bytes-3d.txt, 11-16 05:43 .. 11-19 05:12), computed every hour:

| rule | mean hour-to-hour move | highest day | hours under 30 GB/day after the 11-18 22:53 sweep |
|---|---|---|---|
| one sample (today) | 6.91 GB | 84.5 GB | 0 |
| median, 6 h | 3.31 GB | 66.9 GB | 2.5 |
| max, 6 h | 3.28 GB | 48.0 GB | 0 |
| min, 6 h | 3.74 GB | 69.0 GB | 6.1 |

The median halves the jitter, still says the 11-18 day that lost 77 GB by df, and lags a sweep by about half its window. max loses that day, and min holds a sweep's fall for the whole window. 3 h and 12 h windows: in the package.

What changes (crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/disk.rs only):
- day_fall: each end is the median of its window's readings (an even count's median is the mean of the middle two), at the mean of their times.
  - A day ago: the samples carrying a number for storage.free_bytes at or after now less 30 h, and at or before now less 24 h.
  - Now: those after now less 6 h and before now, and the free disk now, at now.
  - The fall is the first median less the second, over the days between their times, rounded, in bytes a day (below zero when the disk gained, as today).
  - None when the window a day ago holds no reading or there is no free disk now. That replaces "none without a sample a day old within 36 h".
- The module's note says it.
- Nothing else changes: the fit, worse() and its basis words ("fit", "day"), days_left, grew_most (the fit's), the readings, and every other figure.
- No new store read: the week's samples are read once already and the day's fall filters them.

The owner part (the lead's three conditions):
- rsi/scenarios/222.sh asserted the one-sample rule's figures. They change to the windows' figures, each named in the package README with old -> new and why, and as tight as before (within 2 GB):
  - (1) 80 GB -> 70.625 GB a day (a day ago F + 80 - 10 x 2.5/24 at 26.5 h; now F + 80 x 2.5/24 at 2.5 h);
  - (1b) the gap 23-29 h -> 23-28 h (the window a day ago reaches 30 h, so it keeps one reading, 29 h old), and 62 -> 63.02 GB a day;
  - (5) 25 GB -> the windows' figure for the hour the scenario runs (25 GB a day when midnight's sample is 6 h old or more, else F + 25 less F + 5 over the days between).
- rsi/scenarios/retired-tests gains disk::tests::the_days_fall_is_from_the_latest_sample_a_day_old_not_the_oldest and the_days_fall_takes_36_hours_exactly_and_nothing_older. Both asserted the one-sample rule; their cases are the new tests'.
- A mutant that reads one sample at each end (the latest a day ago, the free disk now) fails 228.sh.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/serve/core_lines/disk.rs. Owner: rsi/scenarios/228.sh, rsi/backlog/228.json, rsi/scenarios/222.sh, rsi/scenarios/retired-tests.

Tests (unit, disk.rs): the replaced two, and:
- a_gate_holding_trees_at_one_end_moves_the_days_fall_no_more: steady, a 6 GiB dip a day ago, a dip now, and a real 77 GiB fall;
- the_days_fall_ends_are_medians_at_their_mean_times: an even count, and the times' mean;
- the_days_fall_windows_are_six_hours_each: both edges of both windows.
a_days_fall_with_no_fit_is_said keeps its name; its figure is now the windows'. No other test is renamed or dropped.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/228.sh, black box, a real `spawn serve` on its own database, hourly host.core_lines samples planted as a loop records them (222.sh's harness):
- (1) a flat week at F + 50 GB, then falling through the last day to F: disk_fall within 2 GB of 44.79 GB a day, basis "day" (the one sample a day old says 50);
- (2) the same with the sample 24 h old 6 GB lower: within 1 GB of (1)'s, basis "day";
- (3) the same with the sample 1 h old 6 GB lower: within 1 GB of (1)'s;
- (4) (R2) a flat week at F + 50 GB, no sample between 2 h and 23 h ago, the one sample 1 h old at F + 20 GB: now's window is that reading and the free disk now, median F + 10 at 0.5 h; disk_fall within 2 GB of 36.92 GB a day, basis "day". Without the free disk now in now's median, or with the upper of an even count's middle two, it says 28.2 or 27.7.
222.sh's (5) answers "run again" (harness) when midnight's sample is within 2 minutes of 6 h old, as at midnight.
On main a4ac64dc, 228.sh exits 1: (1) says 50 and (2) moves by 6 GB. 222.sh as changed exits 1 on main and 0 on the candidate.

Verified by: after landing, on live, GET /api/core-lines' storage.disk_fall (basis "day") read hourly across a gate moves less than 6 GB between hours with no sweep in them (the lead's or rev-i's look).
